limitations: Requires at least one compliant spoke-to-approved-hub peering; this is not merely an allowlist of already-existing peerings.
Connected is a provider-reported status and can be transiently noncompliant during provisioning or repair.
Does not audit the reverse hub-to-spoke resource, hub gateway-transit settings, forwarded traffic, route tables, effective reachability, or unapproved additional peerings.
vWAN and isolated spokes are excluded only by explicit approved target inventory; no resource-tag heuristic is assumed.
policies.scopeNotes: Landing Zones/Corp, traditional hub-spoke target VNet IDs only. Child enumeration is under each selected spoke and accepts approved remote IDs without dereferencing their subscription. Reverse peering needs a separate scope/control.
policies.name: landingzone-l49-corp-spoke-required-hub-peering

limitations: Evaluates WAF policy resources only, whether or not they are attached; it does not prove a WAF policy exists or is attached (see the Application Gateway WAF presence policy), and inline legacy WAF configuration on an Application Gateway is not evaluated. A missing mode is reported as not Prevention; only an explicit Disabled state is reported.

Prevention mode blocks matching requests; review exclusions, custom rules and tuning before assigning Deny. Detection mode is reported even where new rules are deliberately staged, so use an exemption for staged rollouts.
Does not assess managed rule sets, exclusions, custom rules, request-body settings or logging.
policies.scopeNotes: Landing Zones; evaluates every Application Gateway and Azure Front Door WAF policy under the assignment scope. No resource list is required; use an exemption for a staged Detection-mode rollout.
policies.catalogName: Web Application Firewall (WAF) policy must be enabled for Prevention mode
policies.name: landingzone-l55-waf-policy-prevention-mode

limitations: Evaluates only the subnet-to-NAT-gateway association (natGateway.id). A NAT gateway with no subnet association, and the NAT gateway resource itself, are not reported.

Subnets are evaluated both as Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets resources and inside Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks, following the ALZ subnet-policy pattern, so one subnet can appear as two compliance records.

Other outbound designs (Azure Firewall, load balancer outbound rules, public IPs) and default outbound access are not assessed. Deny blocks new or changed associations; existing associations are not removed.
policies.scopeNotes: Landing Zones; evaluates every subnet under the assignment scope. Use assignment exclusions only for approved exceptions; the customer standard is no NAT gateway anywhere.
policies.catalogName: Audit NAT Gateways should not be associated to subnets
policies.name: landingzone-l56-nat-gateway-subnet-association

limitations: Audits NIC association, not creation of an unattached Microsoft.Network/publicIPAddresses resource.
All standalone NICs are checked, including NICs not yet attached to a VM; this preserves coverage of NIC creation before VM creation.
Azure Firewall and Application Gateway use their own frontend resource properties and do not require exceptions from this NIC-only policy.
NIC-based appliances need explicit excludedNetworkInterfaceIds or a separately approved assignment exemption.
VM Scale Set instance public-IP configuration requires a separate resource-specific policy.
Audit does not prevent attachment. Deny only affects evaluated new or updated NIC configurations; it does not detach existing public IPs.
policies.scopeNotes: Landing Zones management group. Inherit to Corp and Online; approve NIC-based appliance exceptions explicitly.
policies.name: landingzone-l54-audit-vm-nic-public-ip
